note: Generated by `go test ./internal/compose/ -run TestTheMCPToolCoverageIsPublished -update-mcp-tool-coverage`; do not edit by hand. It reads the use-case lane only — the scenarios under e2e/llm/scenarios and the verdicts the lane commits beside them. A tool counts as DRIVEN when at least one case REQUIRES it (must_call); a case that merely permits a tool (may_call) can pass without ever calling it, so permission is not coverage. Token counts are the budget page's own, one tool rendered alone.

judge_trial_excluded.judge/a verdict from another model is a: the case pins a model with no recorded corpus and asserts the replay is refused; an eval drives the suite live, where there is no replay to mismatch, so it fails for every model alike and measures the trial rather than the judge

criteria.name: A pre-authorized import is actually committed
criteria.statement: The person says they have been through the file and asks for it to go in, so stopping at the dry run to ask for permission already given is the work handed back.

criteria.name: What landed is reported from the run's own report
criteria.statement: How many rows landed and whether anything was skipped, taken from the report rather than assumed from a commit that answered without a failure.

criteria.name: Promises come back as suggestions
criteria.statement: Only what was actually promised is reported. Listing every topic that was discussed means the reader is reciting what it saw rather than what was committed to.

criteria.name: The assistant says what is waiting
criteria.statement: Work held for approval is reported as pending. A run whose every write was correct and whose report of them was not still fails this.

criteria.name: Every figure in the document is the database's
criteria.statement: The report is composed from a saved analytics run and cites the cells holding its numbers, rather than being written around figures the assistant read once and retyped.

criteria.name: A refused literal is not a missing capability
criteria.statement: Being refused a number written into a block says nothing about whether the product can produce a report, and the assistant must not turn that refusal into a conclusion that it cannot.

criteria.name: The forecast is read, not assembled
criteria.statement: The period's expectation comes from the forecast, which applies the installation's fiscal calendar and currency, rather than from a total summed beside it.

criteria.name: The deal with no amount is named
criteria.statement: A deal carrying no amount is real pipeline contributing zero money, and an answer quoting the total without saying so is arithmetically correct and tells the reader something false about what it covers.

criteria.name: Source health is read rather than assumed
criteria.statement: What the nightly check could actually open is looked up, rather than inferred from an empty findings list.

criteria.name: An unread source is not reported as a quiet one
criteria.statement: A source nothing was read from is reported as unread: a quiet week and a broken connector are indistinguishable from inside the numbers, and only one of them is good news.

criteria.name: Real openings, from the host's own calendar
criteria.statement: Times a person can actually offer come back, worked out from the host's calendar rather than described in general terms.

criteria.name: The other side's calendar is not claimed to be known
criteria.statement: Availability answers for one host and not for the invitee, and the assistant must not report the slots as times both people are free.

criteria.name: A possible duplicate is reported, not just filed
criteria.statement: The create's own answer carries the duplicate it queued, and the assistant reads what came back and says so — a queue nobody is told about is a queue nobody reads.

criteria.name: The word the workspace already has is reused
criteria.statement: The user asks for a tag by a spelling the workspace does not hold while it holds a near one, and applying a tag never coins a word — reading the vocabulary and using what is there, rather than adding a second spelling beside it, is the test.

criteria.name: A word that does not exist is coined before it is applied
criteria.statement: Applying a tag is refused for a name the workspace does not have, so the new word has to be created first; an answer reporting records tagged with a word nobody coined is reporting a write that was refused.

criteria.name: The retired word on the record is reported
criteria.statement: A record's own row omits archived tags, so an answer drawn from the record alone says the retired word is not there — reading the record's tags, where a retired word still shows, is the test.

criteria.name: One record loses the word and the word survives
criteria.statement: The tagging comes off the single account named and the vocabulary is left alone: retiring the word for the whole workspace answers a question nobody asked and takes it from the accounts that hold it honestly.

criteria.name: The surviving word is chosen by what carries it
criteria.statement: Which of two duplicate words survives is decided by how many records each is on, and only the tag's own read carries that count — the tag list does not.

criteria.name: A fold nobody has released is reported as waiting
criteria.statement: Folding one word into another is a person's decision, and the answer names that decision rather than describing the vocabulary as already tidied up.

criteria.name: The surviving word is given its meaning
criteria.statement: The description that stops a third spelling being coined is written onto the word that survives, not left as a sentence in the reply.

criteria.name: The duplicate is merged, and which record survives is said
criteria.statement: The second card carries correspondence worth keeping, so it is folded into the record that survives rather than archived where that history is stranded — and because the fold cannot be called back the other way round, the survivor is named rather than left for the reader to guess.

criteria.name: The company that shut down is archived, not merged
criteria.statement: The closed account has no twin to fold into and nothing worth moving, so retiring it is what takes it out of day-to-day work; a merge would need a survivor that does not exist.

criteria.name: The account is handed to a named colleague
criteria.statement: Moving the surviving account onto a colleague's book needs that colleague's seat id, which no record carries and no contact search answers.

criteria.name: The numbers are shown before anything is committed
criteria.statement: What the import will do is reported before it is done — how many rows will land, said out loud rather than discovered after the write.

criteria.name: The row that could not be used is reported
criteria.statement: The file carries a row the import cannot take, and the answer says so; a row dropped without telling anyone is a loss nobody can see.

criteria.name: The record decides which verb, not the request
criteria.statement: The request names no lead and no tool and states three policies, so which of the three terminal outcomes each lead gets has to be read off that lead's own record.

criteria.name: What was filled and what is still missing are both reported
criteria.statement: Qualification fills only what the lead's own data implies and names the rest as gaps: an answer reporting the fill without saying a human still has to supply the title has answered half of it.

criteria.name: A terminal verb lands on the lead it belongs to
criteria.statement: Promotion and disqualification are opposite readings of one queue, and the lead that replied and the lead whose address bounced must not be swapped.

criteria.name: How it moved is a different question from where it stands
criteria.statement: The phase history is asked for and only the project's own page carries it; the current phase alone is not an answer to how the project got there.

criteria.name: What is still open is said before the project is closed
criteria.statement: A project closed over an outstanding commitment nobody mentioned is a loss the reader cannot see.

criteria.name: The transport is named as the installation names it
criteria.statement: The conversation is filed as a message on the transport that carried it, carrying the provider value this installation registered rather than a spelling that happens to look right.

criteria.name: Not being able to send is not the same as not being supported
criteria.statement: A transport that can carry no reply still captures, files and reads, and reporting the first as the second tells the reader the product cannot do what it has just done.

criteria.name: Nearby is worked out to be a distance search
criteria.statement: The request names no company, no address and no tool, and the assistant has to find that the workspace can be searched by proximity rather than reporting that it cannot.

criteria.name: Check with the owner before turning up
criteria.statement: The assistant tells the rep to confirm with the account owner rather than acting on a proximity answer alone.

criteria.name: A briefing arrives without naming a record
criteria.statement: The request identifies an account by something other than its name — "Vietnam partner" is not the account's name — and finding it is the test.

criteria.name: The people are named, not their seats
criteria.statement: The briefing names the people on the other side of the meeting rather than describing the roles they hold.

criteria.name: The unkept promise is noticed
criteria.statement: Somebody said they would send something and there is no record it went. Reading across the timeline to spot the gap is the point.

criteria.name: The past cases are found without being named
criteria.statement: The question describes what happened and names no account, so working out which accounts it happened to is the test.

criteria.name: The record's date wins over the prose recalling it
criteria.statement: Where a note's prose and the record it recalls disagree about when something happened, the answer carries the date the record holds.

criteria.name: The disagreement is pointed out, not quietly resolved
criteria.statement: The answer says that the note and the record do not agree, rather than picking one and leaving the reader unaware there was a conflict.

criteria.name: The counts asked for come back as counts
criteria.statement: The question asks for a breakdown by a dimension whose name the assistant is never told, and the answer is the numbers from the report that holds them.

criteria.name: A refusal is not reported as a missing capability
criteria.statement: Being refused a wrong argument name says nothing about what the workspace can answer, and the assistant must not turn it into a conclusion that the CRM cannot break the question down.

criteria.name: The staged change is read, not just listed
criteria.statement: The queue's line is a summary with its values cut short, so an answer reporting what a proposal would do has to open the item itself; a report assembled from the listing is a report of half a sentence.

criteria.name: Each verdict lands on the item it was given for
criteria.statement: Two proposals and two opposite instructions, so approving the one that was to be rejected is a write nobody asked for — and the tool names alone cannot tell the two apart.

criteria.name: The decision is taken, not handed back
criteria.statement: The person gave an explicit approve and an explicit reject, and an assistant that returns the queue and sends them to the web app has reported a limitation this surface does not have.

criteria.name: A misfiled message is moved, not also-linked
criteria.statement: The default is to add the new link beside the old one, and the person asked for the mail to be off the wrong company — an association leaves the wrong timeline still showing it.

criteria.name: A picked set moves as one act
criteria.statement: Three activities named for one destination move all or nothing, rather than as three separate moves of which the second can fail with the first already applied.

criteria.name: History is re-filed, never re-written
criteria.statement: Recording the event again on the right record leaves two events where there was one and the wrong record still holding the first: the association changes and the content does not.
